createOrReplace.title: Pax Silica: India Signs 10-Nation AI Supply Chain Pact
createOrReplace.html:
Pax Silica is a US-led coalition to secure the supply chains behind AI: chips, critical minerals, energy, advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure. On 15 November 2026, India and nine other governments signed its San Francisco Declaration and agreed to set up five working groups. For India, which imported $12.62 billion of integrated circuits in April–December 2025 alone, the pact is about who it can rely on for chips.

The timing matters. India formally joined Pax Silica in February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi. Nine months later the group has moved from a statement of intent to working structures. Meanwhile India's own chip plants are only starting to ship, and electronics exports are rising faster than the domestic supply of the parts inside them. Operators in electronics, auto, telecom and industrial equipment should read this as a sourcing story, not just a diplomatic one.

TL;DR

  • 10 governments, including India, the US, Japan and the UK, released the Pax Silica declaration on 15 November 2026.
  • India's 12 approved semiconductor projects add up to ₹1.64 lakh crore of investment, according to PIB.
  • Integrated circuits became India's third-largest import at $12.62 billion in April–December 2025.
  • Electronics exports rose 24% to $47.96 billion in FY26, led by smartphones.
  • Fab Economics estimates 85% of a fab project's cost is still imported, falling only to 55% by 2035.

What did India sign in San Francisco?

India signed the San Francisco Declaration, a Pax Silica text that treats the supply chains behind advanced AI as shared security infrastructure. It was signed on 15 November 2026 at a founders' retreat in San Francisco.

According to the PTI report carried by Business Standard, 10 governments released the declaration: the US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the UK. The meeting was convened by US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg. The State Department said that less than a year after its December 2025 launch, Pax Silica is "entering a new phase".

The declaration proposes five working groups: pro-innovation policy frameworks; AI adoption in key sectors; supply chain cooperation across the AI stack; safe harbours and supply chain security hubs; and security and resilience. Angel One reported that Helberg expects Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission to join later.

Why does Pax Silica matter for India's AI supply chain?

It matters because India's AI and electronics growth still runs on imported chips, tools and materials, and Pax Silica is a framework for keeping those inputs flowing from trusted partners.

NewsBytes reported that integrated circuits became India's third-largest import, at $12.62 billion between April and December 2025, and that the government expects that bill to climb in FY27. Every AI server, smart meter, EV controller and factory PLC sold in India depends on that supply. The pact sits alongside other recent commitments: Analytics India Magazine reported that the Quad partners planned more than $85 million in technical and financial assistance for trusted AI technologies across the Indo-Pacific, and Angel One reported a separate US commitment of $10 million for critical-minerals recycling infrastructure in India and ASEAN.

How far has the India Semiconductor Mission got?

The India Semiconductor Mission has approved 12 manufacturing projects worth about ₹1.64 lakh crore, but most are still being built, and only a few have started shipping.

PIB data shows the 12 projects comprise one fab, two compound semiconductor fabs and nine packaging units. The May 2026 approvals, two Gujarat units at Dholera and Surat, added ₹3,936 crore. PIB said two projects had started commercial shipments and two more were expected to follow soon. The original mission launched in 2021 with a ₹76,000 crore incentive package, Business Today reported, and the Union Budget 2026-27 announced ISM 2.0.

The AI side is funded separately. IANS reported the IndiaAI Mission outlay at ₹10,372 crore, with a shared compute facility of over 45,000 GPUs. Those GPUs are exactly the kind of hardware Pax Silica aims to keep in trusted hands.

Is India's chip import dependence falling?

It is falling, but slowly: Fab Economics estimates 85% of a fab project's cost is imported today, dropping to 68% by 2030 and 55% by 2035.

The same estimates, published by Business Today, put the imported share of wafer fabrication cost at 50% today, 30% by 2030 and 18% by 2035. Kearney expects only around 10% of specialty gases and chemicals to be made in India by 2030, with near 100% of tools, parts and silicon wafers still imported. Fab Economics estimates India may need about $80 billion in government incentives through 2035, including a $15 billion ISM 2.0 tranche, to build a full ecosystem. The global chip industry is expected to cross $1 trillion by the end of the decade.

What do India's electronics exports tell us?

They show India assembling and exporting far more electronics than before, while the chips inside are mostly still bought abroad.

KNN India reported that electronics exports rose 24% to $47.96 billion in FY26, from $38.56 billion in FY25. Smartphone exports grew nearly 22%, and US imports of Indian smartphones jumped 86% to $19.68 billion. Business Today put FY26 smartphone exports at ₹2.6 trillion ($29.4 billion), with iPhones at ₹2 trillion, over 75% of the total. Loaded PCB exports reached $1.61 billion. Under the PLI scheme, ₹15,554 crore of incentives have been disbursed, and around 59 companies reported ₹2.45 lakh crore of incremental production in April–December 2025. IANS values India's electronics industry at ₹13 lakh crore.

Should Indian manufacturers change sourcing plans now?

Not overnight, but they should map where their chips and modules come from, because Pax Silica will shape which suppliers are treated as trusted over the next few years.

The declaration sets up working groups, not tariffs or bans, so nothing changes on the invoice tomorrow. What changes is direction. Trusted-sourcing language tends to show up later in government procurement rules, export-customer audits and financing terms. A firm that can show which country made each critical part, and has a second source, will be easier to buy from. Here is a practical sequence:

  1. Build a part-origin register. List every chip, module and board in your top products with supplier, country of fabrication and packaging, and lead time.
  2. Flag single-source parts. Mark anything with one supplier or one country of origin, and rank by revenue at risk.
  3. Qualify a second source for the top five flagged parts, preferring partners in Pax Silica countries or Indian ISM packaging units as they come online.
  4. Connect the register to ERP and procurement. Origin data in a spreadsheet goes stale; it needs to sit next to purchase orders and BOMs.
  5. Prepare for audits. US buyers took $19.68 billion of Indian smartphones in FY26; expect more of them to ask for supply chain provenance.
  6. Track the working groups. Assign one person to follow Pax Silica and ISM 2.0 announcements each quarter.

What this means for Indian businesses

For most Indian firms, Pax Silica is not a chip-making decision. It is a data problem: knowing what is inside your products, where it came from and how fast you can switch. The companies that can answer those questions in minutes, not weeks, will win the export orders and government tenders that start asking. From the way we build supply chain and procurement software, the gap is rarely strategy; it is that BOM, supplier and origin data live in different systems. Frequently asked questions

What is Pax Silica?

Pax Silica is a US-led coalition, launched by the US State Department in December 2025, to secure the supply chains behind AI. It covers semiconductors, critical minerals, energy, advanced manufacturing and AI infrastructure. India joined in February 2026, and 10 governments signed its San Francisco Declaration on 15 November 2026.

Which countries signed the San Francisco Declaration?

According to the PTI report, the declaration was released by the US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the UK. US officials expect Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission to join later. The declaration sets up five working groups on policy, adoption, supply chains, security hubs and resilience.

Does Pax Silica change import duties on chips?

No. The declaration announced on 15 November 2026 sets up working groups and shared principles; it does not change tariffs or import duties. Its effect on Indian businesses is likely to come later, through trusted-supplier rules in procurement, export-customer audits and investment flows into partner countries, including India's own chip projects.

How much has India invested in semiconductor plants?

According to PIB, the India Semiconductor Mission has approved 12 projects with cumulative investment of around ₹1.64 lakh crore: one fab, two compound semiconductor fabs and nine packaging units. Two had started commercial shipments by May 2026. The first phase of the mission came with a ₹76,000 crore incentive package.

What should a mid-size manufacturer do about Pax Silica?

Start with visibility. Build a register of every critical chip and module with supplier and country of origin, flag single-source parts, and qualify second sources for the riskiest ones. Link that data to your ERP and purchase orders so you can answer a customer's provenance question quickly. Then review it every quarter as the working groups publish guidance.
